evidence.title: Emdash Claude provider-key authentication

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Tasks
evidence.locator: Creating a Task; Worktrees; After Starting
evidence.finding: A task starts from a branch, issue or pull request with a name (or generated name) and a provider; no preset is required. By default each task gets its own git worktree and branch; worktrees can be disabled or an existing workspace used. Saved conversations and running processes have different lifetimes; tmux keeps terminal and TUI-agent sessions.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Providers
evidence.locator: Supported Providers; Feature Support; Remote agents
evidence.finding: 35 detected agent CLIs. Resume, hooks (working, awaiting input, done) and auto-approve are each supported by a listed subset of providers. Some provider CLIs require account authentication or product access before Emdash can run them. Remote agents must be installed and authenticated on the remote host; preferences are remembered per agent and machine; Chat UI or TUI is chosen in the agent selector.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Passing Issues
evidence.locator: Create from an Issue; Supported Trackers; Connecting Your Tracker
evidence.finding: Tasks can be created from Linear, Asana, Monday.com, Trello, GitHub, Jira, GitLab, Plane, Forgejo, Featurebase, Plain or Notion issues. The linked issue stays attached and inserted context includes provider, identifier, title, URL, description, status, assignees and project; the generated context can be reviewed or edited before sending. Trackers connect with personal API keys or tokens; GitHub uses the project's GitHub account.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Project Settings
evidence.locator: What you can configure; Share settings with your team; Project environment variables; Lifecycle scripts
evidence.finding: Per-project GitHub account, worktree directory, remotes, tmux, agent git credentials, environment variables, preserve patterns (copy .env-style files into new tasks), shell setup and prepare/setup/run/teardown scripts. Scripts, preserve patterns and shell setup can be shared through .emdash.json; for remote projects they run on the remote machine. Env vars are personal settings; credentials should not go in a committed .emdash.json. Run script logs show in the terminal drawer; EMDASH_PORT and a Docker Compose example support services.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Installation
evidence.finding: Emdash runs agents through their official CLIs. Users add a local project, clone a GitHub repository or connect a remote machine. Emdash works locally without signing in or connecting GitHub; GitHub and tracker integrations are optional.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Automations
evidence.locator: Create an automation; Where it runs; Review runs
evidence.finding: Automations run an agent prompt on a cron schedule in a project's new worktree, existing workspace or repository root. For remote projects the Workspace Server owns scheduling and execution and the desktop need not stay connected; a stopped machine cannot run. Run history shows timing, status and errors.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: GitHub Accounts
evidence.locator: Connect GitHub; Manage Accounts; Project Selection; Git authentication
evidence.finding: Multiple GitHub accounts can be connected (Emdash account/OAuth, GitHub CLI import or device flow) and each project selects one for issues, pull requests (create, list, merge), checks and repository creation. Agent git credentials can use that account, system credentials or none.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Remote Development
evidence.finding: The Emdash UI stays on the laptop; repositories, worktrees, agents, terminals, lifecycle scripts, search and scheduled automations run on the SSH machine through the Workspace Server. Agent CLIs and credentials must be installed and authenticated on that machine. A banner advertises Emdash 2.0 early access.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Manage Machines
evidence.locator: System; Workspaces and conversations; Agents, MCP and skills; Automations
evidence.finding: The System tab shows connection, resource usage and dependencies and installs, starts, restarts, shuts down or updates the Workspace Server. A Conversations tab lists agent sessions on the machine. Subscription readings are in Settings, Usage. Closing the desktop does not stop remote automations.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Remote Projects and Tasks
evidence.locator: Open a project; Create a task; Agents, files and tools; Previews and reconnects
evidence.finding: Remote projects can pick, clone or create a GitHub repository. Tasks use a new worktree, existing workspace or repository root; tasks in the same directory share files. Local files and pasted images are uploaded into remote terminals; chat attachments are stored on the target machine. Tmux keeps processes across disconnects but not a reboot.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Connect a Machine
evidence.finding: Add a machine in Settings, Machines with an SSH alias or host details (password, key or agent auth), test it, then install or start the Workspace Runtime from the System tab and add a remote project. Hosts need SSH, Git and the development tools.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Tmux Sessions
evidence.finding: Tmux keeps terminal and TUI-agent processes and history on the host across closed views or lost SSH, but not through a host reboot or explicit termination. Chat UI history and provider resume are separate.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Diff View
evidence.finding: The Pull Requests section shows PR files, commits, checks, comments and merge state for the task branch. Commit offers Commit, Commit & Push or Commit & Create PR; the footer shows fetch, pull, push and publish actions.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: CI/CD Checks
evidence.finding: The Checks tab lists GitHub check runs for the PR head with status, source, duration and links, and shows PR comments below them.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: In-App Browser
evidence.finding: An in-app browser previews task dev servers. Remote previews forward the remote port to the laptop automatically or through Forward Port with an optional local port; no tunnel lifetime or access control is documented.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: File Editor
evidence.finding: The file editor offers syntax highlighting, find/replace, tabs and language intelligence (definitions, references, diagnostics) in local and SSH workspaces.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Keyboard Shortcuts
evidence.finding: Default shortcuts such as Cmd+N create task, Cmd+J terminal drawer, Cmd+Shift+B browser and Cmd+Shift+1 changes panel; most can be rebound in Settings.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: MCP Servers
evidence.locator: Adding a Server from the Catalog; Editing and Removing; Catalog Servers
evidence.finding: MCP servers are added from a 54-server catalog (including Context7 and Exa) or as custom stdio/http servers, with required credentials entered in the modal, and synced into each selected agent's native config. Remove deletes a server from all agents.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Prompts
evidence.finding: Saved prompts can be edited or deleted from the library and inserted into task conversations.

evidence.title: Emdash docs: Skills
evidence.finding: Installed skills can be uninstalled, removing them from ~/.agentskills and the agent symlinks.

evidence.title: What's next for Emdash
evidence.finding: Emdash 2.0 (coding agents for whole teams) is in early access with a work-email waitlist. The current desktop app is renamed Emdash Classic; it stays open source and keeps getting fixes. No end date is given.

evidence.title: Emdash Classic changelog
evidence.finding: v1.2.10: long workspace operations no longer fail after 30 seconds; credential tokens and environment values stay out of process arguments. v1.2.9 adds GitLab repository creation and merge request workflows. Retrieved 2026-11-21, the page's newest entry is v1.2.10.

evidence.title: Emdash v1.2.11 release notes
evidence.finding: Project Git credentials apply to Emdash's own push, pull and fetch; users can join the Emdash 2.0 waitlist from the sidebar.

evidence.title: Emdash v1.2.12 release notes
evidence.finding: Waitlist signups go to emdash.com; importing data from Emdash v0 runs in one transaction.

evidence.title: Emdash Workspace Server package and repository license (v1.2.13)
evidence.finding: The Workspace Server daemon lives in apps/workspace-server of the same repository, declares Apache-2.0 and has no separate license file; the root LICENSE.md is Apache-2.0 (General Action, Inc.).

evidence.title: Emdash desktop source: bounded billing search (v1.2.13)
evidence.locator: search of apps/ and packages/ for stripe, checkout, purchase, billing and credits
evidence.finding: No purchase, billing or credit-sale code exists in the Classic desktop or Workspace Server; credit matches are wire flow control and an MCP catalog description.

evidence.title: Emdash archiveTask and restoreTask (v1.2.13)
evidence.finding: Archiving sets archivedAt and reaps the task's tmux session and agent process while keeping the worktree and session id; restoreTask clears archivedAt so the task can resume.

evidence.title: Emdash search service (v1.2.13)
evidence.finding: The app search index holds projects, tasks (with branch) and conversations, updated on create, rename, archive and delete; archived tasks leave the index.

evidence.title: Emdash automation scheduler (v1.2.13)
evidence.locator: DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS line 17; queueDueRuns and worker loop lines 206-264
evidence.finding: Due automation runs are marked queued and started only while running workers are below maxConcurrentRuns (default 4); others wait in the queue.

evidence.title: Emdash merge UI state and footer (v1.2.13)
evidence.locator: canBypass line 27; BLOCKED and pending-check states; merge-footer.tsx bypass checkbox
evidence.finding: For GitHub PRs that are blocked, behind or waiting on checks, Emdash offers merging only after ticking 'Merge without waiting for requirements to be met (bypass rules)'; GitLab gets no bypass. Whether the bypass succeeds is decided by the Git host. A bounded search of source-control, github and agent/issue plugin code for deployment found no deployment status tracking.

evidence.title: Emdash diff line comments (v1.2.13)
evidence.finding: Draft line comments attach to working-tree, PR or commit diffs and can be inserted into an agent conversation through the Diff comments mention.

evidence.title: Emdash provider usage probes (v1.2.13)
evidence.finding: Usage probes report account, plan and usage windows with percent used and reset time; probes are implemented only for Claude Code and Codex.

evidence.title: Emdash v0 data import (v1.2.13)
evidence.locator: legacy-port importers: projects, tasks, conversations, ssh-connections
evidence.finding: The desktop detects an Emdash v0 database and imports its projects, tasks, conversations and SSH connections.

evidence.title: Emdash issue provider capability (v1.2.13)
evidence.finding: Issue providers implement listIssues, searchIssues and optional getIssue only; a bounded search of the provider implementations found no create, update, comment, transition or POST/PATCH/PUT calls.

evidence.title: Emdash per-provider settings (v1.2.13)
evidence.finding: Settings are stored per host and provider: Chat UI (ACP) keeps the provider's own option values; TUI (PTY) keeps an autoApprove flag that defaults to false.

evidence.title: Emdash conversation model (v1.2.13)
evidence.finding: Each conversation in a task has its own providerId, pty or acp transport, session id, model, agentStatus and agentStatusSeen flag, so a task can hold conversations with different agents.

evidence.title: Emdash ACP chat store (v1.2.13)
evidence.locator: permissionQueue and queuedPrompts; edit/delete queued prompt
evidence.finding: Chat UI queues prompts sent while the agent is busy (editable and deletable) and surfaces provider permission requests in a queue the user answers.

evidence.title: Emdash agent status and attention events (v1.2.13)
evidence.finding: Agent status is idle, working, awaiting-input, error or completed; permission, idle and elicitation hook notifications count as attention and drive needs-attention sounds and notifications.

evidence.title: Emdash v1.2.13 telemetry consent and README
